issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Farm to use a List (specifically an ArrayList) to hold animals, but the provided solution uses a Set (HashSet) for the animals attribute. The template Farm.java also lacks the animals field and constructor initialization expected by the instructions. This mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about the intended collection type and API (List vs Set) and about how to implement get/set methods and iteration order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize it as an ArrayList in the Farm() constructor (and provide get/set returning List<Animal>), or revise the problem statement/UML to specify a Set if uniqueness/no-order is intended. Also ensure the template Farm.java includes the animals field and constructor signature that match the chosen collection type so students can follow the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs that the Farm should use a List (implemented with an ArrayList) to store its animals, referring to the collection as a List/ArrayList (e.g., 'animals: List<Animal>' and 'Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor'). The reference solution, however, implements the same conceptual entity as a Set (private Set<Animal> animals, using HashSet). Using different collection type identifiers for the same conceptual entity (the Farm's animals collection) creates a mapping mismatch: students are told to implement an ArrayList but the canonical solution uses a HashSet/Set, which may confuse students comparing their implementation to the solution or following the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to use List<Animal> and initialize an ArrayList in Farm() (e.g., private List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>();) to match the problem instructions, or update the problem statement and any templates to accept/describe Set/HashSet instead of List/ArrayList so students and the solution use the same identifier for the collection type.
